title: Higher Order Function Challenge Solution
summary: Solution page for the four-operation calculator challenge from the previous lecture. The page body was only an 'Open' link-out, so this note is built from the reference repo's finished code.

concepts.heading: Solution structure
points: (Extra) Four operator functions (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) each take num1 and num2 and return the result of one arithmetic operator.
(Extra) calculator(num1, num2, operator) is the higher order function: it simply returns operator(num1, num2), so the caller chooses the behaviour by passing a function name.
(Extra) Call sites pass the function name without parentheses. Adding parentheses would invoke the function early with no arguments.
(Extra) Division by zero in JavaScript gives Infinity rather than an error; there is no guard in the solution.
